hypotheses.text: The topographic selectivity of muscle degeneration in LGMDR29 (SNUPN deficiency) is fundamentally invariant to age of onset, with axial (paravertebral) and specific distal (peroneal and medial gastrocnemius) involvement occurring subclinically or clinically in childhood-onset cases rather than being restricted to adult-onset presentations.
hypotheses.rationale: Resolves the contradiction in the binned hypothesis claiming childhood onset is 'purely proximal limb-girdle weakness'. While clinical manifestation in children is described primarily as proximal weakness, muscle imaging reveals identical axial and selective distal lower limb involvement across both pediatric- and adult-onset cohorts.

evidence.text: Five patients with childhood-onset limb-girdle muscular dystrophy showed predominant MRI impairment of paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, peroneal, and medial gastrocnemius muscles.

source.title: Biallelic variants in SNUPN cause a limb girdle muscular dystrophy with myofibrillar-like features
source.quote: SNUPN patients show a similar phenotype characterized by proximal weakness starting in childhood, restrictive respiratory dysfunction and prominent contractures, although inter-individual variability in terms of severity even in individuals from the same family was found... MRI showed predominant impairment of paravertebral, vasti, sartorius, gracilis, peroneal and medial gastrocnemius muscles.

evidence.text: Two adult-onset siblings presented with proximo-distal and axial weakness with early respiratory impairment, demonstrating MRI fat replacement in paravertebral, triceps brachii, sartorius, and gracilis muscles.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
source.quote: Two siblings carrying two novel deleterious variants in the SNUPN gene (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) showed adult-onset proximo-distal and axial muscle weakness with early respiratory involvement... Muscle MRI identified involvement in the paravertebral, triceps brachii, sartorius and gracilis muscles.

hypotheses.text: Adult-onset SNUPN-related myopathy is distinguishable from sporadic inclusion body myositis (sIBM) by the preservation of the deep finger flexors and the presence of selective sartorius and gracilis muscle degeneration on MRI.
hypotheses.rationale: Muelas et al. (2026) report that adult-onset SNUPN muscular dystrophy presents with proximo-distal and axial weakness mimicking IBM. Testing specific differences (e.g., gracilis/sartorius involvement vs. IBM's typical sparing of gracilis/sartorius and classic finger flexor weakness) establishes clear phenocopy discriminators.

evidence.text: Adult-onset SNUPN patients presented with clinical features reminding inclusion body myositis (IBM), but muscle MRI showed prominent sartorius, gracilis, paravertebral, and triceps brachii involvement.

source.quote: We advise SNUPN testing in patients with late-onset proximo-distal and axial weakness with early respiratory impairment and features reminding inclusion body myositis (IBM).

hypotheses.text: Pediatric-onset SNUPN deficiency comprises an atypical, multisystem muscular dystrophy distinct from classical isolated limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, distinguished by early neurological co-morbidities and neurodevelopmental defects.
hypotheses.rationale: Contradicts the notion that early-onset disease represents a 'pure proximal limb-girdle muscular dystrophy', demonstrating that early presentations frequently present as syndromic/complex neuromuscular entities.

evidence.text: A cohort of 18 children from 15 unrelated families with biallelic SNUPN variants presented with atypical muscular dystrophy and associated neurological defects.

source.title: SNUPN deficiency causes a recessive muscular dystrophy due to RNA mis-splicing and ECM dysregulation
source.quote: In this study, we investigate 18 children from 15 unrelated families who present with atypical muscular dystrophy and neurological defects.

evidence.text: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy encompasses phenotypes ranging from pure childhood-onset muscular dystrophy to complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia.

source.title: SNUPN‐Related Muscular Dystrophy: Novel Phenotypic, Pathological and Functional Protein Insights
source.journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
source.quote: SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy or LGMDR29 is a new entity that covers from a congenital or childhood onset pure muscular dystrophy to more complex phenotypes combining neurodevelopmental features, cataracts, or spinocerebellar ataxia.

new_directions.question_text: Does early respiratory failure out of proportion to ambulatory loss serve as an invariant clinical hallmark across both pediatric- and adult-onset LGMDR29?
new_directions.rationale: Both Iruzubieta et al. (2024) and Muelas et al. (2026) report early or restrictive respiratory involvement, which could distinguish SNUPN-related dystrophy from many other LGMDs that spare respiratory function until non-ambulatory stages.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact histopathological differences on electron microscopy and immunostaining that separate adult-onset SNUPN deficiency from inflammatory inclusion body myositis?
new_directions.rationale: Muelas et al. (2026) identified granular deposits suggestive of biomolecular condensates and nuclear envelope/sarcolemma remodelling, which could offer decisive pathological markers for biopsy differentiation.
